item.title: Despite financial and logistical challenges, Taveuni rugby teams ready for Skipper Cup
item.description: Speaking to fijivillage Sports during their training session at Albert Park in Suva, Assistant Coach Alusio Vakaoqotabua says the team's preparations began back in the village before travelling to Viti Levu for the final stages of training. The Taveuni Men’s and U20 squads arrived in Suva last night and they have settled in well at the St Peters Chanel Parish Hall in Delainavesi.
item.content:encoded:
Speaking to fijivillage Sports during their training session at Albert Park in Suva, Assistant Coach Alusio Vakaoqotabua says the team's preparations began back in the village before travelling to Viti Levu for the final stages of training.

The Taveuni Men’s and U20 squads arrived in Suva last night and they have settled in well at the St Peters Chanel Parish Hall in Delainavesi.

Vakaoqotabua says one of the biggest challenges has been the lack of training equipment and limited finances, but the coaches and players remained determined to keep preparing for the competition.

Insert: coach on challenges, 27th July 26

He says while the Fiji Rugby Union has provided financial assistance, the team still had to work hard to meet the costs of its campaign.

To help cover additional expenses, the players and officials organised fundraising activities and received strong support from the people of Taveuni.

Vakaoqotabua says that encouragement from back home has kept the team motivated throughout their journey and inspired the players to keep pushing through the challenges.

He says today's training session is part of the team's final preparations before Saturday's games at Lawaqa Park, where both the Under-20 and senior teams will take on Malolo.

Vakaoqotabua is calling on Taveuni supporters living around Viti Levu to come out in numbers and cheer on the team.

He says the players are determined to give everything they have on the field to make their families, villages and everyone back home in Taveuni proud.

item.title: Navosa to face Yasawa in Ranadi Cup final
item.description: Navosa will face Yasawa in the Royal Tea Ranadi Cup after both teams won their respective semi-final matches. Navosa secured a hard-fought 33-31 victory over Navosa in the first semi-final.
item.content:encoded:
Navosa will face Yasawa in the Royal Tea Ranadi Cup after both teams won their respective semi-final matches.

Navosa secured a hard-fought 33-31 victory over Navosa in the first semi-final.

The match was fiercely contested from start to finish, with both teams matching each other's blow for blow and keeping spectators on the edge of their seats throughout the full 80 minutes.

The Vanua Levu side showed greater determination in the closing stages, capitalizing on opportunities created by Navosa's handling errors and maintaining pressure whenever chances came their way.

Registrations open next week for Rexona Suva Marathon 2026
item.description: The marathon will be held on Saturday, 8th August, starting and finishing at the Albert Park Pavilion in Suva. Participants can choose from the full marathon, half marathon, 10-kilometre race or the popular Team Marathon.
item.content:encoded:
The marathon will be held on Saturday, 8th August, starting and finishing at the Albert Park Pavilion in Suva.

Participants can choose from the full marathon, half marathon, 10-kilometre race or the popular Team Marathon.

Registrations opened on Wednesday, 1st July through TicketMax and are open to people aged 14 years and over.

The Team Marathon will again feature two categories, with the Social League encouraging families and friends to complete the course together, while the Business League is designed for corporate teams.

Entry fees are $70 for the full marathon, $50 for the half marathon, $15 for the 10-kilometre event, $50 for the four-person Social League Team Marathon and $80 for the four-person Business League.

The Suva Marathon has become one of Fiji's biggest annual running events, attracting experienced runners, first-time participants, families and corporate teams from around the country, as well as overseas competitors .

The event is supported by naming rights sponsor Rexona, through the Motibhai Group, major sponsor Munro Leys, and several other sponsors and partners.

Organisers say the marathon builds on the success of the Namosi Challenge and continues to encourage more people to embrace running and lead active, healthy lifestyles.

item.title: Brad Mooar appointed Head Coach of the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua
item.description: The Fijian Drua have appointed former All Blacks Brad Mooar as Head Coach of the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua ahead of the 2027 Shop N Save Super Rugby Pacific season. Mooar has signed a two-year contract and will officially begin his role in September this year to prepare the team for the 2027 season.
item.content:encoded:
The Fijian Drua have appointed former All Blacks Brad Mooar as Head Coach of the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua ahead of the 2027 Shop N Save Super Rugby Pacific season.

Mooar has signed a two-year contract and will officially begin his role in September this year to prepare the team for the 2027 season.

The championship-winning Crusaders coach and former All Blacks and Scotland assistant coach was selected following an extensive global recruitment process involving Fijian Drua and Fiji Rugby leadership, along with an independent expert.

The Drua say Mooar impressed the selection panel with his vision of combining Fiji's exciting style of rugby with the discipline, consistency and physicality needed to compete successfully in Super Rugby Pacific.

Mooar is currently an assistant coach with the Crusaders, having returned to the franchise for the 2025 and 2026 seasons.

During his previous stint with the Crusaders from 2016 to 2019, he helped guide the side to three consecutive Super Rugby titles.

He also served as Head Coach of Welsh club Scarlets before joining the All Blacks as backs and attack coach and later worked with Scotland during the 2023 Six Nations Championship and Rugby World Cup.

Fijian Drua Chief Executive Officer Jeff Miller says Mooar stood out during an exceptionally competitive recruitment process because of his technical and tactical knowledge, experience in championship-winning environments, ability to develop playe rs and build strong relationships.

Miller says Mooar also understands the Drua's purpose extends beyond winning matches, with the club aiming to inspire the nation and create positive change through rugby.

Mooar says it is a tremendous honour to lead Fiji's Super Rugby Pacific team and he is excited to work with Fijian players and become part of the Drua family.

He says there is enormous potential to build a successful and entertaining style of rugby that will inspire the country while competing for championships.

Mooar also congratulated the McDonald's Fijian Drua Women after they finished as minor premiers and secured a home Super Rugby Women's Grand Final, praising the players and coaching staff for their historic achievement.

The Fijian Drua say further announcements regarding the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua Men's coaching group will be made in due course.

item.title: Ba stays top of Extra Premier League after 4-1 win over Lautoka
item.description: Ba FC has maintained its place at the top of the Extra Premier League standings after thrashing Lautoka FC 4-1 yesterday. The victory sees the Men in Black remain at the top of the table with 33 points, one point ahead of second-placed Labasa FC, who edged Navua FC 1-0.
item.content:encoded:
Ba FC has maintained its place at the top of the Extra Premier League standings after thrashing Lautoka FC 4-1 yesterday.

The victory sees the Men in Black remain at the top of the table with 33 points, one point ahead of second-placed Labasa FC, who edged Navua FC 1-0.

Rewa FC remains in third place with 29 points after playing out a 1-1 draw with Nadi FC.

Meanwhile, Nadroga FC defeated Nasinu FC 1-0, while Tailevu Naitasiri FC claimed a thrilling 3-2 win over Suva FC.

With just three rounds remaining in the Extra Premier League season, the race for the league title is heating up as teams also look to build momentum heading into one of Fiji's most prestigious football tournaments, the Extra Battle of the Giants.

Ba, Labasa, Rewa, Lautoka, Navua, Suva, Nadi and Nasinu have all secured their places in the tournament.

Nadi has bounced back strongly after missing out on the BiC Fiji FACT earlier this season to secure its place in the Battle of the Giants.

Meanwhile, Nadroga and Tailevu Naitasiri have missed out after finishing outside the top eight and will not feature in this year's tournament.

The Battle of the Giants pool matches will be played from 4th to 6th September, with the semi-finals and final scheduled for the following week at 4R Stadium, Govind Park.
